item.title: Xi urges actively addressing population aging
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
BEIJING, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged further efforts to implement the national strategy of actively addressing population aging and to ensure happier and more fulfilling lives for elderly people. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on work related to aging. Since the 18th National Congress of the CPC in 2012, China has made fresh progress in responding to population aging, with both elderly care services and the elderly care industry developing at a rapid pace, Xi said. Xi emphasized the importance of coordinating efforts among the government, market, society and families and further strengthening social security, elderly care services, health services, and social participation for older people. He also stressed the need to boost the silver economy and build an age-friendly society. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on aging held from Wednesday to Thursday in Beijing. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended and delivered a speech at the meeting. Li stressed the need to take a balanced perspective on the far-reaching implications of an aging population, be fully aware of China's unique advantages in addressing this demographic shift, and act with a stronger sense of responsibility and greater proactivity to advance work in this area. With the goal of enhancing the wellbeing of elderly people, efforts should be made to meet their needs for a better life and deliver on key tasks concerning elderly people, Li said. China has the world's largest elderly population. By the end of 2025, China had 323.38 million people aged 60 and above, or 23 percent of the population. The figure is projected to exceed 400 million by around 2035.

item.title: Xi meets Trump, calling for continued efforts to steer China-U.S. relations on right course
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, calling for continued efforts to jointly steer the giant ship of China-U.S. relations in the right direction toward the future. Trump is in the southern Chinese city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi said that China-U.S. relations have generally maintained a stable and positive trajectory, bringing tangible benefits to people of both countries and injecting stability and certainty into the world. Xi said that he and Trump had jointly explored the right way for China and the United States, as two major countries, to get along, established a new vision to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and given it new substance grounded in respect, fairness and reciprocity. The new vision has been welcomed by the people of both China and the United States, as well as the international community, he added. Xi stressed that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented and pioneering endeavor, adding that the key to sustaining the current positive momentum lies in taking concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state. The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability. Xi called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns, and work toward mutual benefit. The cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity. China and the United States should strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence (AI) and ensure that AI always remains under human control, he said. On the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations, Xi said. Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of U.S.-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger. Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted. He called on both sides to maintain the positive momentum of the stable development in bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence. The United States does not support "Taiwan independence," Trump said. He congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability.

item.title: Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace. Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Xi said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among themselves, but should hold the line on peaceful coexistence and make efforts to avoid the Thucydides Trap. As the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, Xi said. He said that nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, combine their respective strengths as major countries in resources, manufacturing and consumption, so as to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go. Xi said that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. Full text: Remarks by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting

item.title: Xi says China-Russia-U.S. Shenzhen Summit of groundbreaking significance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state is of groundbreaking significance. Xi made the remarks at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province.

item.title: Chinese police chief meets Malaysian home affairs minister
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
SHENZHEN, Nov. 18 -- Chinese State Councilor and Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong on Wednesday met with Minister of Home Affairs of Malaysia Saifuddin Nasution Ismail in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wang noted that the Chinese side stands ready to work with Malaysia to step up joint efforts to combat transnational crimes and advance the development of the International Alliance Combating Telecom and Cyber Fraud. The alliance was inaugurated in China in September this year. He also called for stronger cooperation in key areas to further enhance bilateral law enforcement and security cooperation. Saifuddin expressed his willingness to maintain close communication with the Chinese side and further advance law enforcement and security cooperation between the two countries.

item.title: Chinese vice premier stresses high-quality development in east China's Jiangxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
NANCHANG, Nov. 18 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang has called on Jiangxi Province in east China to build on its distinctive strengths, foster new growth drivers and achieve new progress in high-quality development. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the comments during a research tour of the province from Monday to Wednesday this week. He first visited a site in Yudu County, where the Central Red Army had assembled ahead of the Long March. Noting that this year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March, Ding urged carrying forward the great spirit of the Long March, steadfastly advancing high-quality development, and continually meeting the people's growing aspirations for a better life. Ding visited a primary school and a local company in Yudu to learn about efforts to improve basic education and the development of key local industries, and heard suggestions on promoting the revitalization of old revolutionary base areas. He called for ensuring that old revolutionary base areas are not left behind in the modernization process, developing county-level economies, expanding employment opportunities and increasing local residents' incomes, consolidating and building on the gains made in poverty alleviation, addressing gaps in infrastructure and public services, and improving the quality of basic education, so as to steadily improve people's lives. He also visited a university laboratory and local companies in Jiangxi to learn about scientific research and industrial development. High-level sci-tech innovation platforms should be established and resources pooled to advance basic research and original innovation to meet the country's urgent needs and long-term priorities, Ding said. He called for building on local research capabilities and industrial foundations, leveraging comparative advantages, developing new quality productive forces in light of local conditions, and fostering new drivers of economic growth. He stressed the need to deepen the integration of sci-tech innovation and industrial innovation, and strengthen innovation capabilities to support the steady and sound development of China's sci-tech finance sector.

item.title: Chinese premier urges China, ASEAN to stand united, overcome distractions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
MANILA, Nov. 16 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Monday that in a turbulent and complex world, China and ASEAN should stand united, overcome distractions and work together to build a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. Li made the remarks during the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila. As this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that over the past five years, the world has witnessed a growing trend of unilateralism and protectionism, while geopolitical conflicts have flared up one after another. Against this backdrop, China-ASEAN cooperation has forged ahead, achieving both quantitative growth and qualitative improvements, with cooperation mechanisms further consolidated and connectivity steadily enhanced, he said. The extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons, Li said. He stressed that both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development. These experiences and lessons are a valuable asset shared by both sides and should be upheld and put to full use over the long term, Li said. Five years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed that China and ASEAN work together to build a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home, Li said, adding that both China and ASEAN countries cherish the culture of family and are geographically close and bound by strong people-to-people ties. The profound bonds forged over generations should not, and will not, be affected by temporary events or circumstances, he said. Li urged China and ASEAN countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village. He called on the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. China looks forward to the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea, which will provide a solid institutional guarantee for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea, Li said. He also called for promoting regional development and prosperity, stressing the need for both sides to take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity," in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules. The premier said China applauds the establishment of a China-ASEAN mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with ASEAN to successfully hold the China-ASEAN Year of artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation next year, advance "AI+" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development. Li also called for improving the well-being of the people, voicing China's readiness to continue to contribute to the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund and strengthen cooperation with ASEAN in areas including poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation, food security, maternal and child health, so as to promote sustainable development in the region. Commending the fruitful outcomes achieved over the five years since the establishment of the ASEAN-China comprehensive strategic partnership, leaders of ASEAN countries expressed readiness to strengthen strategic communication and political mutual trust with China, fully implement the ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and deepen cooperation in areas including economy and trade, connectivity, AI, clean energy, digital economy and combating transnational crime. They thanked China for its consistent support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture and its commitment to the peaceful settlement of disputes. They also expressed the hope for an early conclusion of the COC in the South China Sea, jointly safeguarding regional peace and stability, and building an ASEAN-China community with a shared future. It was announced during the meeting that the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will enter into force on Dec. 1, 2026, and 2027 has been designated as the Year of AI cooperation. Outcome documents were released, covering the 5th anniversary of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, energy partnership building, and deeper forestry cooperation. Full Text: Remarks by Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the 29th China-ASEAN Summit

item.title: Chinese premier signs decree to revise, repeal certain administrative regulations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 -- A decision by China's State Council to amend and repeal certain administrative regulations was made public on Thursday. Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating the decision, which aims to address pointless formalities to lighten the burden on those working on the ground, implement the reform of Party and state institutions, and ensure the consistency of relevant laws and regulations. Certain provisions of 14 administrative regulations were revised, and four regulations were repealed, according to the document. The State Council decided to revise a regulation on river course administration to align it with related provisions in the country's Ecological and Environmental Code. Meanwhile, a regulation on the limits of liability for maritime passenger transport between Chinese ports was repealed to better meet the needs of ongoing reform and development, and address practical realities in relevant areas. The decision takes effect on the date of its promulgation.
